body.statement: The certificates \((g_2,\pi_2)\) and \((g_4,\pi_4)\) are primal-dual saddles for both observation maps. In particular, \[\rho_2^{\mathrm{CR}}=\rho_2^W=\frac14,\qquad \rho_4^{\mathrm{CR}}=\rho_4^W=1-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.\] Every response-type state outside the displayed prior supports has risk strictly below the corresponding saddle value under the displayed rule.
body.justification: The two smallest admissible populations establish that posterior relevance of the second count does not by itself imply minimax value.
body.gap: No located complete-randomization minimax paper reports unrestricted full-count and difference-only equality at these exact finite sizes.
body.consumer: The result provides regression tests for exact minimax implementations at the two smallest balanced sample sizes.
body.proof_tex:
All calculations in this proof use the kernel derived in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}response\mbox{-}type\mbox{-}minimax\mbox{-}games}\), rather than a labeled-assignment enumeration.

For \(n=2\), insertion of \(g_2(0)=0\) and \(g_2(\pm2)=\pm1/2\) into the hypergeometric risk gives the exhaustive table
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{risk}&\text{number of states}&\text{states at risk }1/4\\ \hline
1/4&3&(0,2,0,0),(0,0,2,0),(1,0,0,1)\\
1/8&4&\text{none}\\
0&3&\text{none}.
\end{array}
\]
The multiplicities sum to \(\binom{5}{3}=10=|\mathcal N_2|\), so this is exhaustive and \(\max_NR_N^W(g_2)=1/4\).  The weights of \(\pi_2\) are positive and sum to one.  Its only positive-predictive-mass full-count cells are \((1,0)\) and \((0,1)\).  At the first cell, the target numerator and predictive denominator are, respectively,
\[
 \frac14\cdot1\cdot1=\frac14,
 \qquad
 \frac14\cdot1+\frac12\cdot\frac12=\frac12,
\]
and hence the posterior mean is \(1/2=g_2(2)\); symmetry gives \(-1/2=g_2(-2)\) at the second cell.  Thus \(g_2\) is the full-count Bayes action under \(\pi_2\).  Every support-state risk is \(1/4\), so its full-count Bayes risk is \(1/4\).  The primal and dual inequalities from the preceding theorem give
\[
 \frac14\leq\rho_2^{\mathrm{CR}}\leq\rho_2^W\leq\frac14.
\]
The seven states outside the prior support have risk \(1/8\) or zero, strictly below \(1/4\).

For \(n=4\), put \(S=\sqrt3\), \(z=(3-S)/2\), and \(r=1-S/2\).  The inequalities \(1<S<2\) imply \(0<z<1\).  Direct algebra gives
\[
 (1-z)^2=r,\qquad \frac{z^2}{3}=r.
\]
The first is the risk at each pure-effect state \((0,4,0,0)\) and \((0,0,4,0)\).  At \((2,0,0,2)\), the kernel puts masses \(1/6,2/3,1/6\) on \((2,0),(1,1),(0,2)\), respectively, so its risk is \(z^2/3=r\).

For an exhaustive primal check, substitution of the same kernel into all \(\binom73=35\) response-type states produces exactly the following risk multiset:
\[
\begin{array}{c|r@{\qquad}c|r}
\text{risk}&\text{multiplicity}&\text{risk}&\text{multiplicity}\\ \hline
1-S/2&3&25/32-3S/8&4\\
11/16-S/3&2&43/96-5S/24&4\\
3/8-S/6&4&1/16&4\\
1/24&1&1/32&8\\
1/48&2&0&3.
\end{array}
\]
The multiplicities sum to \(35\).  The greatest inactive entry is \(25/32-3S/8\), and its exact slack is
\[
 r-\left(\frac{25}{32}-\frac{3S}{8}\right)
 =\frac{7-4S}{32}>0,
\]
because \(7>4\sqrt3\) follows after squaring from \(49>48\).  Direct subtraction, using \(5/3<S<7/4\), places every remaining displayed entry below that one or directly below \(r\).  Thus precisely the three stated support states attain \(r\).

Let \(h=(S-1)/4\), the mass on each pure-effect state.  Then \(h>0\), \(z>0\), and \(2h+z=1\).  The only positive-predictive-mass full-count cells under \(\pi_4\) are \((2,0),(1,1),(0,2)\).  The posterior mean at \((1,1)\) is zero, while at \((2,0)\) it is
\[
 \frac{h}{h+z/6}=z=g_4(4),
\]
where the equality is equivalent to \(h(1-z)=z^2/6\), which follows by substituting \(S^2=3\).  Symmetry gives \(-z\) at \((0,2)\).  Hence the posterior mean agrees with \(g_4\) on every positive-predictive-mass full-count cell; the value \(g_4(2)=1/4\) is a feasible completion on prior-null cells.  The prior-average risk is \(r\), because every support state has risk \(r\).  Therefore
\[
 r\leq\rho_4^{\mathrm{CR}}\leq\rho_4^W\leq r,
\]
which proves both asserted equalities and all strict inactive-state claims.
